scope: Proposition 5.1 (Relative null-layer obstruction) of the manuscript “Parabolic intersections in Artin groups” (preprints/Parabolic-intersections-in-Artin-groups-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 254 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4cd7fa316371447c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let I ⊆ S be nonempty and connected, let cI > 0 satisfy CIcI = 0, and extend c by zero outside I. Let J ⊆ I be spherical, possibly empty, let q ∈ Z, and fix AJ x. Suppose its fixed data on (I \ J) ∪ ∂I are capped at q and satisfy mq (I\J)∪∂I = c (I\J)∪∂I . (5.1) It is impossible that every representative z ∈ AJ x capped at q on I satisfies mq j(z) > cj for every j ∈ J. (5.2) Thus, if J ̸= ∅, some such representative has mq j(z) ≤ cj for at least one j ∈ J. If J = ∅, the exterior hypotheses themselves are impossible.
